text:
Last season Kent Johnson had 22 points in 76 games. This season he has 17 in 17. The difference is mostly opportunity: he plays 17:57 a night, up from 13:14, and is on the ice for 80% of Columbus's power-play time, up from 37%. The Athletic also says the numbers make him the league's top shootout artist.

Some of it will not last. He is shooting 21% after 6% last season, with 8 goals on 5.0 expected. His own chances are up, to 0.99 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.69, but not by as much as his goals. Seventeen games is a small sample, and ice time settles faster than scoring.

The timing has been excellent: his goals rank 12th of 522 skaters in our wins added. The five-on-five picture is weaker. Columbus gets 46.6% of the expected goals with him on, and Evolving-Hockey had his offensive impact in the bottom 6% of forwards last season.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found 52% of his shots came off the rush. Our projection has him finishing between 46 and 69 points. What to watch: whether the power-play role survives the first cold week.
